summary: Sweeping a band round a few things and pressing Delete is now one press of Command Z to get them all back. It used to take two: the first press handed back only the dotted outline and left your work deleted, which looked exactly like undo refusing to help.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next. Nothing to switch on.

try.do: Open a new document and drop two screenshots onto it, well apart.
Press V for the pointer, then drag a band across empty canvas so it fully surrounds both.
Press Delete. Both go, and the band comes down.
Check the Layers list: both rows are back, in the order they were.
Press Command Shift Z to redo. Both go again, in one press.
Press Command Z once more, then click one of the pictures and drag it, to be sure the pictures that came back are really usable.

evaluate: Does one press feel like enough, or did you instinctively reach for a second?
Coming back, the dotted band is on screen again but nothing is picked. Does an empty band read as leftover clutter, or as a useful place marker?
Should the two pictures come back already picked, so you can immediately move them or delete them again?
Do the pictures land in exactly the spots and the stacking order you remember?
rough: The band comes back around the restored pictures but they are not picked again, so pressing Delete straight after the undo does nothing. That is how undoing a delete has always behaved here, so it was left alone rather than changed on a bug fix, but it is the one part of the flow that still feels short.

Stacking a marquee band still has the same two-press problem this fixed for deleting: one Command Z gives back only the band and leaves the stack made. Reproduced with the probe and filed as its own p1 rather than folded in here.
